# Pagination

> Animated pagination for React and shadcn, with a width that never changes as you page.

- Docs and live demo: https://eased.dev/components/pagination?ref=context7
- Source: [src/registry/eased/pagination/](../../src/registry/eased/pagination/)
- Installs: `components/eased/pagination/pagination.tsx`
- npm dependencies: `motion`

## Install

```bash
npx shadcn add @eased/pagination
```

Or by URL:

```bash
npx shadcn add https://eased.dev/r/pagination.json
```

Import paths below assume the default `@/components` alias in `components.json`.

Numbered pages with ellipses, previous and next, and a selected chip that glides between pages on a spring. Controlled or uncontrolled, buttons or real links.

## When to use

- Moving through a long, ordered set one page at a time: invoices, search results, an audit log.
- When people need to know where they are and jump to a page, not only "load more".
- The `compact` variant ("Page 3 of 12") for table footers, cards and narrow screens.

## When not to use

- Feeds people skim top to bottom: load more on scroll instead.
- Two to five views of the same thing: use [Segmented](https://eased.dev/components/segmented?ref=context7) or [Tabs](https://eased.dev/components/tabs?ref=context7).
- Steps in a flow with an order to finish: use a stepper.

## Usage

```tsx invoices-pager.tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Pagination } from "@/components/eased/pagination/pagination";

export function InvoicesPager() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
  return <Pagination count={11} page={page} onPageChange={setPage} aria-label="Invoice pages" />;
}
```

## Examples

### Compact

Previous, the page number (it rolls) and next. Reach for it under about 400px, or when the count matters more than the jump.

```tsx
<Pagination variant="compact" size="sm" count={11} page={page} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

### Links

`getHref` renders real `<a>` elements, so pages can be crawled and opened in a new tab. Each link still calls `onPageChange`.

```tsx
<Pagination count={24} page={page} getHref={(p) => `/blog?page=${p}`} />
```

### More context around the current page

```tsx
<Pagination count={40} defaultPage={18} siblings={2} boundaries={1} />
```

## API reference

### Pagination

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | `number` | | How many pages there are. |
| `page` | `number` | | The current page, from 1 (controlled). |
| `defaultPage` | `number` | `1` | The starting page (uncontrolled). |
| `onPageChange` | `(page: number) => void` | | |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "compact"` | `"default"` | Numbered pages, or "Page 3 of 12". |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` | 32px for tables and cards, 36px for pages. |
| `siblings` | `number` | `1` | Pages either side of the current one. |
| `boundaries` | `number` | `1` | Pages always shown at each end. |
| `getHref` | `(page: number) => string` | | Render links instead of buttons. |
| `getPageLabel` | `(page: number) => string` | `` `Page ${p}` `` | Each page's accessible name. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `"Pagination"` | The landmark's name. |
| `className` | `string` | `""` | Appended to the `nav`'s classes. |

Other `nav` props pass through. `paginationSlots(page, count, siblings, boundaries)` is exported for building your own layout.

## Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Moves through previous, each page and next. |
| `←` / `→` | Moves focus to the previous or next control in the row. |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Goes to that page. Focus follows the page if it moved to another slot. |

## Accessibility

- A `nav` landmark named by `aria-label`; the current page has `aria-current="page"`.
- Previous and next at the ends are `aria-disabled`, not `disabled`, so focus is never dropped from under the keyboard.
- Ellipses are hidden from screen readers; the compact variant announces "Page 3 of 12" from a polite live region that stays mounted.
- Targets are 32 or 36px and sit edge to edge with a 4px gap, so they carry no extended hit area.

## Motion

The selected chip is the shared Indicator: it glides to the new page on the snappy spring and redirects mid-flight. Past seven pages the row has a fixed number of slots, so its width never changes; when the window shifts under the chip, each slot's number slides 8px in the direction of travel with a 2px blur (snappy in, 100ms out). Page numbers press by colour only, never scale, so the chip measures them true; previous and next press like icon buttons. The compact number rolls. Reduced motion: the chip jumps and numbers change in place.

## Notes for AI

Use Pagination when a list is split into numbered pages the server or client already knows the count of. Wire `page` and `onPageChange` to your data fetch, or `getHref` for URL-driven pages; use `variant="compact"` in table footers and below 400px.

Don't hide previous and next at the ends or add your own selected style or animation to the page buttons: the chip, the slot swap and focus handling are built in. Hide the whole control yourself when there is only one page.
